The Owls were pegged by sportsbooks, modelers, and pundits as one of the worst teams in the country, but they defied all of those predictions with a 10-win season that culminated with them defeating Jacksonville State in the Conference USA Championship Game. Unfortunately, all that success meant the sharks were circling, and Kennesaw State lost several key players to the transfer portal this offseason. Thus, it's no surprise that the Owls have sputtered to a 1-4 start in 2026. That said, they should have a decent chance to build some momentum against Missouri State on Wednesday night. The Bears are regrouping after a decisive 34-13 road loss to Western Kentucky, while the Owls hope to rebound from a heartbreaking 27-26 defeat at the hands of Jacksonville State. The Bears surrender 449.6 total yards and 32.4 points per game, and they get gashed on the ground specifically, allowing 196.4 rushing yards at 4.77 per carry. Rickie Collins is the engine for Kennesaw State. Boogie Woods III and Latrelle Murrell combine to average 5.2 yards a carry, which is exactly the profile you want against a front allowing almost 200 rushing yards per game. picks.blurb: The Kennesaw State Owls (1-4, 0-1 CUSA) won this league last year and were expected to contend for the title again, but they've had a disappointing start to the year and have dropped back-to-back one-score games. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Last week, they lost to a Western Kentucky game that looked like it could be the worst in the conference. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. Still, he's the driving force behind this offense considering he also leads the way in a quarterback-centric rushing attack. That offense is a strength relative to the defense, which has been pretty rough overall, particularly against the pass. Missouri State's offense has its own issues, though, and it benched quarterback Skyler Locklear for Henry Belin IV last week. Still, this is an offense that doesn't run or pass particularly well, and its defense is arguably an even bigger weakness. It's hard to have much faith in Missouri State here, given how uncompetitive it was against Western Kentucky. Can the Buckeyes avenge last year's Big Ten Championship loss? One of the biggest games of the college football season is set for Saturday afternoon as No. 4 Ohio State travels to Bloomington to take on No. 5 Indiana in FOX's Big Noon Saturday showdown. And there is plenty of bad blood between these two programs. The last time these teams met, Indiana stunned Ohio State 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten Championship Game, ending the Buckeyes' undefeated season. Now, Ryan Day and Ohio State have an opportunity to return the favor against Curt Cignetti's defending national champions. Ohio State enters at 5-1, while Indiana remains undefeated at 6-0. Both teams are 3-0 in Big Ten play, making this matchup potentially decisive in the conference championship race. Ohio State: Can Julian Sayin Deliver? Ohio State's offense has been explosive this season, averaging more than 42 points per game. Quarterback Julian Sayin has thrown for approximately 1,772 yards, while superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has been nearly unstoppable, recording 48 receptions for 916 yards and 11 touchdowns. Smith is the most dangerous player in college football, and Indiana's secondary will have its hands full trying to contain him. However, last year's championship game exposed some serious problems for Ohio State. Sayin threw for 258 yards, and Smith recorded eight catches for 144 yards, but the Buckeyes managed just 10 points. Sayin was also sacked five times. Indiana's defensive front remains dangerous, averaging 3.3 sacks and 8.2 tackles for loss per game this season. Running back Bo Jackson, who has rushed for approximately 460 yards, must help establish balance and prevent Indiana from focusing entirely on Sayin. Indiana: The Hoosiers Aren't Going Anywhere Indiana might have lost Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza, but Curt Cignetti has kept the Hoosiers rolling. TCU transfer Josh Hoover has thrown for more than 1,300 yards with 17 touchdowns and zero interceptions, while running back Turbo Richard has rushed for nearly 600 yards. Wide receiver Charlie Becker has also been outstanding, recording 529 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. Michigan State transfer Nick Marsh gives Indiana another dangerous weapon on the outside. Defensively, Indiana is allowing approximately 12 points per game and has demonstrated an ability to create pressure without sacrificing coverage. However, the Hoosiers haven't exactly dominated their recent competition. Indiana narrowly escaped Northwestern 29-23 before defeating Nebraska 20-17 last weekend. Those performances raise questions about whether the Hoosiers can consistently move the football against an elite opponent. Expect another physical, defensive battle between two legitimate College Football Playoff contenders. Pete Fiutak Wed, October 14, 2026 at 6:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just a few weeks ago, Florida was coming off a 52-28 obliteration of a terrific Ole Miss team, and everything was wonderful. The Gators appeared good enough in the first season under Jon Sumrall to be in the SEC and College Football Playoff mix, the offense was unstoppable, and then a funny thing happened. The SEC figured it out. Missouri and South Carolina beat Florida by a combined score of 83-36, and now, with the schedule ahead, the 4-2 team might have to fight just to get to a bowl game. Last week at this time, Texas was No. 1, it was about to play a punchless Oklahoma team, and then a funny thing happened. The Sooners came up with creative and clutch ways to pull off a 27-24 Red River Rivalry win. The season is hardly over for the Longhorns, but now there's little margin for error over a tough second half. Florida vs Texas: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for Florida after this, with a week off before dealing with Georgia, followed up by Oklahoma, and then a trip to Kentucky. Texas starts a run of three straight home games, getting Ole Miss next and Mississippi State to follow. How is this only the sixth game between these two? Texas is 3-1-1, with the 7-7 tie coming in the first meeting in 1924. How To Watch Florida vs Texas Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ABC Location: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin, TX – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Florida Will Win The defense isn't getting fixed over the next few weeks, but that's part of what a rebuild is all about. The Gators win when the offense rocks, and the yards and points allowed are simply the cost of doing business. However, there's one key element to the Florida D that should show up huge. The pass rush is outstanding. The Gator defensive front averages close to three sacks and seven tackles for loss per game, and as good as Arch Manning is – seriously, he's really good, despite the popular opinions at the moment after the OU loss – he's still not amazing when he's getting rushed. The Texas offensive line has been better than last year for the ground game, but the pass protection has been a problem. Why Texas Will Win The Texas defense is going to stuff the Florida offense cold. Missouri and South Carolina never let Gator star Jadan Baugh and the running game breathe. The Gamecocks and Tigers combined for 18 tackles for loss against the Florida attack, and both allowed fewer than 400 yards of total offense. For all the problems in the meltdown against Oklahoma, the Texas defense was great. It allowed only 238 yards of Sooner offense, and for the fourth game in a row – including against Ohio State and Tennessee – the defense allowed fewer than 100 rushing yards. Florida vs Texas Prediction, Betting Lines It turned out to be one of the most important games of the 2025 season. Florida finished the year 4-8, but one of those wins was a 29-21 thriller over Texas. The Longhorns lost on the road to both Ohio State and Georgia – no shame there against two teams that finished with 12 wins – but that loss to the Gators kept them out of the College Football Playoff. Yeah, Texas lost to Oklahoma, but weird things happen in the Red River Rivalry. Against Florida, the offense will keep it conservative, but Arch will connect on a few deep shots to push ahead. The defense will take care of the rest. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:36 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 7 Texas looks to bounce back against Florida after a devastating loss to Oklahoma. Can Arch Manning silence his critics and save the Longhorns' season? No. 7 Texas (4-1) returns home Saturday afternoon to face Florida (4-2) in a massive SEC matchup between two programs desperate for a bounce-back victory. The Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, while Florida was dominated 38-19 at home by South Carolina. Both teams entered the season with championship aspirations, but another loss could seriously damage their College Football Playoff hopes. And for Texas quarterback Arch Manning, the pressure has never been higher. Texas: It's Time for Arch Manning to Deliver Manning entered the season as one of the Heisman Trophy favorites, but his performances have been anything but consistent. Through five games, Manning has thrown for 1,122 yards, 10 touchdowns, and five interceptions. Against Oklahoma, he completed 19 of 31 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but two costly fourth-quarter interceptions helped the Sooners erase a 17-7 halftime deficit. The Longhorns are averaging just 379.2 yards per game, ranking 79th nationally. That's simply unacceptable considering the offensive talent Steve Sarkisian has assembled. However, Saturday presents an excellent opportunity to get things back on track. Florida's defense is allowing 393 yards and 29 points per game, including an alarming 268.7 passing yards per contest. Wide receiver Cam Coleman, who has 318 receiving yards and five touchdowns, should have opportunities to create explosive plays against a struggling Gators secondary. Defensively, Texas has been outstanding, allowing just 16 points and 96 rushing yards per game. Edge rusher Colin Simmons has been nearly unstoppable, recording 9.5 sacks. Florida: Can Jadan Baugh Save the Gators? Florida's offense has actually been impressive this season, averaging 41.7 points and 473.8 yards per game. Quarterback Aaron Philo has thrown for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns, and three interceptions, while receiver Dallas Wilson has recorded 376 yards and three touchdowns. However, the biggest storyline is running back Jadan Baugh. Baugh has rushed for 672 yards and 12 touchdowns, establishing himself as one of the SEC's most productive backs. Unfortunately, his production has slowed considerably. Over Florida's last two games, Baugh has managed just 72 rushing yards, including 59 yards on 15 carries against South Carolina. That's a major concern considering Texas possesses one of the nation's best rushing defenses. Florida also defeated Texas 29-21 last season, meaning the Gators have already proven they're capable of beating Sarkisian's program. But winning in Austin will be a completely different challenge. How Each Team Wins For Texas, the formula starts with protecting Manning and establishing an early rhythm through the passing game. The Longhorns must take advantage of Florida's vulnerable secondary while allowing their defensive front to disrupt Philo and contain Baugh. For Florida, everything revolves around getting Baugh going early. If the Gators can establish their rushing attack, they'll have opportunities to control possession and keep Manning on the sidelines. Defensively, Florida must force Manning into mistakes, something Oklahoma successfully accomplished last weekend. I expect Texas to respond with a much more disciplined performance following its disappointing loss to Oklahoma. Manning should have opportunities to attack Florida's secondary, but I'm still not convinced he's capable of consistently dominating SEC competition. Expect a solid, rather than spectacular, performance from the Texas quarterback. The biggest difference will be Texas' defense. With Simmons creating pressure and the Longhorns limiting Baugh's rushing opportunities, Florida will struggle to sustain drives throughout the afternoon. I expect the Gators to keep things competitive early, but Texas will gradually take control in the second half. Final Score: No. 7 Texas 27, Florida 17 Texas gets back in the win column, improves to 5-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Florida Gators can put the Texas Longhorns' College Football Playoff hopes on life support this weekend in Austin. Both teams are looking to rebound from losses last weekend. Texas suffered its first loss of the season last Saturday, falling 27-24 to Oklahoma. Florida, meanwhile, has now lost two games after getting upset at home in a 38-19 loss to South Carolina. If Texas loses this weekend, they'll likely need to win out to make the 12-team playoff. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Florida vs Texas ESPN's Greg McElroy made his score predictions for this weekend's biggest games, and he has Texas beating Florida 31-17. "Where does Florida find 21 points?" said McElroy. "Florida scored 17 and 19 in their last two games against SEC defenses. When this (Texas) team allows fewer than 21 points, Steve Sarkisian is 63-4 as an FBS head coach. Now, Florida's best route there is the short field off of a Texas mistake because this Texas defense, they almost never let long drives finish in the end zone. "I'm taking Texas to win the game 31-17. I think Texas will win on third down all afternoon, because Florida's defense is probably going to have a hard time getting off the field, and I think Texas is built to live in short yardage. Florida's offense has stalled the last couple of weeks against SEC defenses, and this is the best defense I think they've seen so far. And that's no disrespect to South Carolina or Missouri — Texas is a step up in competition and personnel. … So we think Texas wins this game by a couple of touchdowns, but I do think both defenses will play well enough to keep it relatively low scoring. Texas wins this one slowly and on schedule. Whether or not we see the offensive fireworks is one of the biggest questions in the game." away.blurb: According to Zenitz, Philo has "been limited" in practice this week as he deals with an injury. If he is unable to play, Zenitz believes backup Tramell Jones would get the start, the first of his career. Florida will release its first availability report ahead of the game on Wednesday night, which should provide more information on Philo's availability. The status of starting quarterback Aaron Philo is uncertain as the Florida Gators prepare for a massive showdown with the Texas Longhorns , according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. Philo, who competed with Jones for the starting job, has started all six of Florida's games this year, completing 105 of his 149 passes (70.4%) for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns, and three interceptions. He has also run for 104 yards and three touchdowns on 44 carries. It is his first season as a starter after he spent the past two seasons as Georgia Tech's backup before following Buster Faulkner to Gainesville this offseason. In four SEC games, he has completed 73 of his 107 passes (68.2%) for 824 yards, four touchdowns, and two interceptions. Jones has played in five games this year for Florida, his second with the team. He has thrown for 252 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions, completing 23 of his 29 attempts (79.3%). He has five carries for 25 yards. away.headline: Florida Gators Injury Report: Buster Faulkner's offense is in serious jeopardy going into Saturday's game vs. Texas Longhorns
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: After winning their first four games, the Florida Gators have gotten blown out their last two games 83-36. It wasn’t that they lost that was the problem; being embarrassed twice, including on homecoming, was a terrible turn for Jon Sumrall . The first injury report for the Gators is out, and it’s not looking good for the offense. We had already learned that quarterback Aaron Philo was limited in practice. He’s not the only key memeber of the offense on the injury report. The other two questionable players were in the same spot at this time last week in wide receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton. Luckily, Brown seems to be looking good in practice this week, and having him back would be huge. The offense has lacked explosiveness without him on the field. Of all the players on the list, the biggest is running back Duke Clark. He’s currently listed as out, which is brutal. He’s the perfect complement to running back Jadan Baugh, giving the Gators that burst in the running game that they have been able to maximize. Not having him could be a big deal come Saturday. The Florida Gators are not in the best position going into a must-win game against the Texas Longhorns. Now, the Gators have the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon, and it’s become a must-win game. They will have a bye week next week before facing the Georgia Bulldogs, and it’s a very real possibility that the Gators are 4-4 going into the month of November. Florida Gators’ offense in dire straits after injury report If the Gators don’t have Philo, Tramell Jones Jr. will get the opportunity to start, and he looked good during the competition. Plus, with the offensive line in the situation it’s in right now, having a more mobile quarterback could be a smart play. The next three days will really tell us how things will be for Buster Faulkner’s offense. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. With the quarterback situation in flux due to Kamario Taylor's apparent turf toe injury sustained against Alabama, State enters the week as two touchdown underdogs on the first fall-like Saturday of football season. Coaches on both sides have a fair amount of familiarity with each other having worked together in Oxford from 2020-21 as boss and apprentice. Can Lane Kiffin and the Tigers bounce back after an embarrassing loss? The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. MSU coach Jeff Lebby has provided few details about Taylor's injury that forced him to watch the fourth quarter of the Alabama game from the sideline with a boot on his right foot. MSU has not said what his exact injury is. The first SEC availability report will release Oct. 14 with nightly updates until 90 minutes before kickoff. It's possible Taylor plays against LSU, but is it worth the risk? And, what if he doesn't play? Does Mississippi State stand a chance to beat LSU? Should Kamario Taylor play vs LSU if he's not healthy? The Bulldogs played Taylor when he wasn't at full speed vs Alabama, and it did not work well. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. No, it's not nearly as fierce as the Iron Bowl when Alabama takes on Auburn, but when you've played 130 times, you tend to have a few interesting moments that build into something generational. Georgia just got by Alabama in a controversial 20-17 thriller – let's just say the Bulldogs got a wee bit of a break on a key Crimson Tide deep shot – and now it's the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn has had two weeks off to get ready for this, and knocking the Bulldogs off of their lofty perch would put the first season under head coach Alex Golesh into hyperdrive. Auburn vs Georgia: Quick Hits Auburn gets LSU and the Lane Kiffin show next, and then goes to Ole Miss. Georgia gets a week off before playing the Cocktail Party showdown against Florida in Atlanta, and then it goes to Ole Miss. Georgia has won seven times in the series since losing in 2017 (it was No. 1 in the nation then, too), but it won the SEC Championship a few weeks later. The Bulldogs have won 11 of the last 12 meetings. It might have been hit hard by Florida, but it does a lot of bending without breaking, thanks to plenty of sacks, lots of plays behind the line, and a third down defense that's holding up well. Offensively, the high-tempo Tiger attack should be able to keep the Bulldogs on their heels. Alabama ran well last week, but it only handed the ball off 29 times. Auburn won't make that mistake, pushing for at least 35 carries, and close to 40, as it tries to hit the Georgia defense with tempo. Why Georgia Will Win Georgia's defensive front will live in the Auburn backfield. It's a problem with Auburn's style that it allows defenses to tee off on the quarterback and come up with too many tackles for loss. The Tigers don't worry about the time of possession battle, and they're good at overcoming negative plays with something positive, but Georgia has the defense to swarm all over the quick-hitting short plays. Auburn doesn't do anything deep, and Georgia should limit any yards after the catch or runs that get to the second level. Auburn vs Georgia Prediction, Betting Lines It's been an interesting start to the Golesh era. The offense is supposed to dominate and take over, but it doesn't do it enough. The defense that was so great last year has stayed strong, but it's about to get pounded on. Auburn's two losses came when it allowed over three yards per carry. Georgia is averaging over six yards per pop. picks.blurb: Georgia football vs Auburn scouting report, bold predictions, injury updates - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Story by Athens Banner-Herald Georgia football vs Auburn scouting report, bold predictions, injury updates Marc Weiszer, Athens Banner-Herald Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:02 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads At the end of a profanity-filled postgame speech leaked after Georgia's football' s win at Alabama Saturday night—audio that Kirby Smart said he preferred had not been put on social media—the Bulldogs coach mentioned building off of it. "This team, man, are you going to take this and grow from it?" Smart said. "The naysayers said they couldn't go there and win and they ain't played nobody." Alabama certainly was a step up in competition, a team the Bulldogs traded haymakers with all night in a 20-17 victory. The challenge for Georgia (6-0, 4-0 SEC) this week is to turn the page from an opponent that now feels like a rivalry to many to one that has been one of the biggest and is its longest in Auburn . This is the 131 st meeting between the schools some 180 miles apart. Auburn (4-2, 1-2) will have a fourth different head coach on the sideline since Smart came aboard in Athens. Smart has gone up against Gus Malzahn, Bryan Harsin, Hugh Freeze and now will face Alex Golesh. The Tigers are ranked No. 33 on ESPN's SP+, which puts it 11 th in the SEC and below an Oklahoma team that Georgia rolled past three weeks ago. The Tigers had an open date on their schedule last week, giving the players a break from the grind and coaches more of a chance to evaluate how to get better. "They're coming off an off week, and we're coming off a really tough physical game," Smart said. "It will be really important that the mindset and the approach to the game is right because they want to make it physical the way they play." Georgia vs. Auburn predictions Georgia is No. 1 ranked for the first time since September of 2024. It moved to that spot a day after top-ranked Texas was upset by unranked Oklahoma. Two other top 15 SEC teams also went down to unranked foes: No. 10 LSU to Kentucky and No. 15 Florida to South Carolina. Smart alluded to those results when talking about the challenge Auburn presents. "They have a lot of talent," Smart said. "They've got good football players, and it's any given Saturday in this conference, as we see every week." Auburn is missing perhaps its most valuable piece. Linebacker Xavier Atkins, a second-team All-American in 2025, won't play. Golesh didn't disclose why saying that would be kept "in-house," and his status would be revisited next week. AuburnSports reported Atkins has had disciplinary issues centered on being late to or missing mandatory meetings and practice habits were also a factor. Georgia players have said putting the last game behind them is just part of what they do. "We try to focus on being consistent," linebacker Justin Williams said. "You know you can't be too high or too low. You have to be right in the middle." Georgia vs. Auburn scouting report Why Georgia has an advantage: Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown ranks 14th in the SEC in passing efficiency and has as many interceptions as touchdowns with 7 each. "We've got the right plan in place to go attack them," he told reporters in Auburn. The Bulldogs defense limited Alabama to 346 total yards. Why Auburn has an advantage: The Tigers have been solid on the back end, ranking 30th in the nation in pass efficiency defense with 6 interceptions and just 4 touchdown passes against. UCLA transfer Andre Jordan has 2 interceptions. Linebacker Elijah Melendez (3 sacks) and Walter Mathis Jr. (2 sacks) from Savannah help apply the pressure. Georgia vs. Auburn injury updates Georgia: Wide receiver Isiah Canion (lower extremity, out), running back Chauncey Bowens (lower body, out), safety KJ Bolden (leg, questionable), wide receiver Thomas Blackshear (collarbone, out), defensive back Tyriq Green (leg, out), offensive lineman Marcus Harrison (undisclosed, probable), RB Dante Dowdell (multiple injuries including collarbone, lung and arm, out), outside linebacker Amaris Williams (knee, out). Auburn: Offensive lineman Tai Buster (undisclosed, out), TE Hunter Herring (undisclosed out), LB Xavier Atkins (non-injury, out). Georgia 37, Auburn 10: Auburn last topped 13 points in a game at Georgia in 2009 when Chris Todd was the quarterback. This doesn't look like a Tigers offense that can change that. It has scored 21 and 14 points the last two games and ranks 13th in the SEC in scoring. Georgia vs. Auburn scouting report: What we're watching Georgia pass rush: Georgia rang up four sacks against Alabama, raising its season total to 17. That's just three shy of what the Bulldogs registered all of last season. Raylen Wilson leads the team with 3, Chris Cole has 2 1/2 and Gabe Harris contributes 2. Cole's 14 quarterback pressures leads the team. Auburn's pace: The Tigers are apt to snap the ball fast, something that Georgia cornerback Demello Jones noted this week. Auburn leads the nation in running a play every 21.5 seconds, the fastest in the nation. "It's something we've got to adjust to," Jones said. "Just us getting lined up on the defensive side, executing calls." Georgia RB Bo Walker: Georgia still is not at full strength in the backfield. Dwight Phillips carried the load at Alabama with 17 rushes for 120 yards but second-year running back Bo Walker had a career-high 10 carries for 69 yards. He showed good vision and big-play ability on a day where his longest run was 37 yards. "He brings a lot," Phillips said. "He's explosive as well." Homecoming game for Auburn tight end: Jake Johnson, in his fifth college season after playing for Texas A&M and North Carolina, returns home to face Georgia. Johnson is the son of former NFL coach Brad Johnson and is the nephew of former Georgia coach Mark Richt. The Oconee County High graduate has 7 catches for 43 yards this season. Bold predictions for Georgia football vs Auburn Georgia will continue ground game momentum: Georgia's offensive line limited Alabama to one sack last week and paved the way for 206 rushing yards. Auburn is 81st against the run nationally at 149 yards per game and gave up touchdown runs of 25 and 44 in its last game at Tennessee. Byrum Brown will make plays with his feet: The South Florida transfer has more rushing yards per game than any quarterback in the SEC with 68.8 per game and has 4 rushing touchdowns. Byrum is a load to bring down at 6-foot-3 and 235 pounds. He rushed for 107 yards at Tennessee on 19 carries. London Humphreys will continue to be key target: After having just four catches in the first four games, the Vanderbilt transfer has 6 catches for 62 yards the last two weeks including a 20-yard touchdown catch at Alabama from Gunner Stockton. Auburn's offensive line will be rattled on the road: In Auburn's only road game this season, the Tigers had a bevy of pre-snap penalties involving four different offensive lineman. Georgia's crowd should be able to cause false starts for the Tigers once again for an offensive line filled with transfers. away.blurb: The remaining SEC teams in the AP Poll are Ole Miss (No. 9), Missouri (No. 13), Tennessee (No. 14), and Mississippi State (No. 16). The last time Auburn played the No. 1 team in the AP Top 25 was in 2023, when it lost to the Georgia Bulldogs 27-20 in Hugh Freeze's first year as head coach. The last time the Tigers defeated the top-ranked team was in 2017, beating Alabama 26-14. Two weeks before that game, Auburn defeated Georgia, 40-17, when the Bulldogs were ranked No. 1. The AP Poll saw some movement outside of Texas dropping six spots. The LSU Tigers fell the farthest, dropping from No. 10 to No. 22 after their 35-34 overtime loss to unranked Kentucky. home.headline: Kirby Smart says Georgia is 'beat up.' Here's the latest on injuries
home.blurb: “We're a beat up football team right now, guys,” coach Kirby Smart said after the 20-17 win over Alabama. “We've got guys out left and right.” Canion was listed as questionable last week on the SEC Availability Report before being downgraded Friday to out. Blackshear is out with a broken collarbone, according to ABC on Saturday night’s broadcast. The average return to play for contact sports for a broken collarbone is 8 to 12 weeks, according to an Instagram post by Dr. Mike Galbraith, a Texas-based sports medicine physician. Freshman Craig Dandridge played a season-high 55 snaps with Blackshear and Canion out. "We had to go all week kind of not knowing on Isiah," Smart said Monday. "How does it affect you? You talk to Mike (Bobo), you talk to the offensive staff, it's frustrating because you don't really know who's in and who's out. You're trying to make decisions. We thought Nate was going to be able to play. That was a surprise to us. Isiah, we knew it would be close, maybe or maybe not. It just makes it hard because you can't get enough reps for guys." Here's the latest on injuries Marc Weiszer Athens Banner-Herald Updated Oct. 12, 2026, 1:25 p.m. ET Georgia football went on the road and beat Alabama Saturday night with running back Dwight Phillips stepping up in a big way as Nate Frazier was unable to go with injured ribs. The No. 1 Bulldogs are dealing with several notable injuries heading into a week seven game Saturday at home against Auburn. Georgia played its third straight game without Isiah Canion, the transfer wide receiver from Georgia Tech who Smart said Monday is dealing with "a lower extremity injury." The Bulldogs were also without wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, who was injured in the win over Vanderbilt on Oct. 3. Phillips rushed for a career-high 120 yards on 17 carries against Alabama with Frazier and Chauncey Bowens sidelined. Bowens leads the team in rushing touchdowns. He sustained an undisclosed injury against Vanderbilt. Frazier missed the Oklahoma game after being injured at Arkansas and returned to get two second-half carries against Vanderbilt. He was not listed on the availability report all last week, but warmed up and did not play Saturday. ABC’s Holly Rowe said he made a quick cutting move and needed attention from the training staff. Phillips was asked Monday if he had an idea that Frazier wouldn’t be able to go or was surprised. “That’s probably a Kirby Smart question,” he said with a smile.

TUSCALOOSA, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 10: Head coach Kalen DeBoer of the Alabama Crimson Tide reacts to a play during the second half of the game against the Georgia Bulldogs at Bryant Denny Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Photo by Butch Dill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brent Taylor Sun, October 11, 2026 at 5:39 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After a close loss to Georgia, Alabama didn't drop in the Coaches Poll Rankings , hanging in at number 7. Essentially, Alabama proved they belong with the elite teams, with a resume boasting a win over the suddenly excellent Kentucky and a loss to #1 Georgia that could have gone either way. The Tennessee Volunteers are similarly 5-1, but it took squeaking out tight wins over SEC bottom feeders Arkansas and Auburn. The Vols have generally played well on defense, but their offense has left a LOT to be desired, with QB Faizon Brandon leading an anemic passing attack until he was injured, and backup George MacIntyre not doing any better. So they're sitting put with a #15 ranking. FanDuel's sportsbook has the opening odds set to Alabama holding a -6.5 favorite over Tennessee, with an over/under of 55.5. Week 1 – Beat Furman 56-9 Week 2 – Beat Georgia Tech 45-24 Week 3 – Beat Kennesaw State 42-9 Week 4 – Lost to Texas 17-20 Week 5 – Beat Auburn 24-14 Week 6 – Beat Arkansas 24-17 The Vols are averaging 22 points per game on offense and 17 points per game on defense in SEC play, with the biggest problem being that, for the season, they're averaging only 187 passing yards per game (and that includes their three warm up games to start the season). Running back DeSean Bishop is still carrying the entire offense with 678 rushing yards. Week 1 – Beat East Carolina 48-10 Week 2 – Beat Kentucky 45-17 Week 3 – Beat Florida State 50-36 Week 4 – Beat South Carolina 49-18 Week 5 – Beat Mississippi State 56-23 Week 6 – Lost to Georgia 17-20 The Tide's offense obliterated all of their first five foes, scoring 45+ in every single game despite having only a single cupcake game. Then Georgia happened, and the two elite squads turned the game into a low-possession, high-stakes contest (seriously, there were only 7 combined drives in the entire second half). The Alabama defense has had some struggles this year. They've been a playmaking defense, but they've also given up some downfield passes in almost every game, and then struggled with UGA's rushing attack last week. Still, the held the Dogs to less than half of their usual offensive output. Alabama boasts a much better offense, but the two teams have likely equivalent defenses. However, the game will be at Neyland Stadium. Still, the 6.5 spread with a 55.5 OU has the prediction something like a 31-25 Crimson Tide victory. How the Tide responds to a tough and disappointed loss in their clash with Georgia will be paramount, but I wouldn't be surprised if this one winds up going under the 55.5 points. Something more like a 21-14 kind of game. What do you think? Give us your thoughts in the comments below.

picks.headline: Alabama @ Tennessee Preview And Prediction
picks.blurb: Alabama @ Tennessee Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Alabama @ Tennessee Preview And Prediction Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre (12) hands the ball to Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop (18) during a college football game between Tennessee and Auburn at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Oct. 3, 2026. Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee for a massive SEC rivalry showdown. Can Keelon Russell bounce back and keep the Tide's playoff hopes alive? One of college football's greatest rivalries returns Saturday afternoon as No. 6 Alabama (5-1) travels to Knoxville to face No. 14 Tennessee (5-1) in the Third Saturday in October showdown. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC, and both programs have plenty to prove. Alabama is coming off a heartbreaking 20-17 loss to Georgia, while Tennessee narrowly escaped Arkansas with a 24-17 victory. The Crimson Tide defeated Tennessee 37-20 last season, but the Volunteers have won the last two meetings in Knoxville. With both teams fighting for College Football Playoff positioning, Saturday's matchup could have enormous consequences. Alabama: Can Keelon Russell Bounce Back? Alabama's offense has been one of the nation's most explosive units, averaging 44.2 points per game. Quarterback Keelon Russell has thrown for 1,599 yards, 12 touchdowns, and just two interceptions while adding 225 rushing yards and four scores. However, Georgia exposed some weaknesses in the sophomore quarterback's game. Russell completed just 16 of 30 passes for 185 yards and one touchdown against the Bulldogs, struggling to consistently move the football against an elite defense. Saturday presents another difficult challenge. Tennessee is allowing just 15.5 points per game and has surrendered only three passing touchdowns through six games. Making matters worse, Alabama is expected to be without leading receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, who has recorded 415 receiving yards and four touchdowns. That means Lotzeir Brooks, who has 389 receiving yards, and Rico Scott will need to step up. The Crimson Tide must also establish their rushing attack to prevent Tennessee from putting all its attention on Russell. Tennessee: The Volunteers Have a MAJOR Problem Tennessee has managed to win five of its first six games, but Josh Heupel's offense has serious questions at quarterback. Freshman Faizon Brandon has battled a shoulder injury, forcing George MacIntyre into his first career start against Arkansas. MacIntyre completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. And against Alabama's talented secondary, those mistakes could prove extremely costly. The Volunteers rank just 110th nationally in passing offense, averaging 186.5 yards per game. However, Tennessee has been outstanding on the ground. Running back DeSean Bishop has rushed for 678 yards and eight touchdowns, helping Tennessee average 228.3 rushing yards per game. Bishop will be the biggest threat to Alabama's defense, especially considering Georgia rushed for more than 200 yards against the Crimson Tide last weekend. Wide receiver Mike Matthews, who leads Tennessee with 396 receiving yards, could also create problems if Alabama becomes too focused on stopping the run. How Each Team Wins For Alabama, the formula starts with forcing Tennessee to throw the football. If the Crimson Tide can contain Bishop and put the Volunteers into third-and-long situations, their defense should have opportunities to create turnovers. Offensively, Russell must protect the football, utilize his mobility, and attack Tennessee's secondary without forcing unnecessary throws. For Tennessee, everything revolves around establishing the rushing attack and controlling possession. The Volunteers must also generate consistent pressure on Russell and prevent Alabama from creating explosive plays downfield. A loud Neyland Stadium crowd could make things difficult for Alabama, particularly if Tennessee establishes an early lead. I expect a physical, defensive battle between two SEC rivals. Tennessee's rushing attack will create problems early, but I don't trust the Volunteers' quarterback situation against Alabama's defense. Whether it's Brandon or MacIntyre under center, Tennessee simply hasn't demonstrated enough consistency throwing the football. Russell should respond with a much cleaner performance after struggling against Georgia, although I don't expect Alabama's offense to put up its usual explosive numbers. The Crimson Tide will establish a narrow lead before halftime and gradually take control in the second half. I expect Alabama's defense to force multiple turnovers, while Russell makes enough plays to secure a comfortable road victory. Final Score: No. 6 Alabama 24, No. 14 Tennessee 13 Alabama gets back on track, improves to 6-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. Tennessee's quarterback struggles ultimately prove too much to overcome. Check Out All EasySportz College Football Content Here! College Football Viewing Guide

Can the Tennessee Vols knock off the Alabama Crimson Tide this weekend? CBS Sports' Chris Hummer is "highly skeptical" that they can. Hummer is predicting that Alabama will beat Tennessee 24-17 on Saturday afternoon in Knoxville. "The Vols have survived this year behind an elite defense," wrote Hummer . "That unit has carried an offense that ranks just 66th nationally in yards per play and 110th in passing yards per game. But is that defense good enough to hold off Alabama? I'm highly skeptical. Hummer's colleague at CBS Sports, Brad Crawford, also has Alabama winning this weekend, though he has the Crimson Tide leaving Neyland Stadium with a 30-17 win. Known as " The Third Saturday in October ," this is a matchup that has produced mixed results in recent years after a dominant decade-plus stretch in the rivalry under former Alabama head coach Nick Saban. The teams have split the last four meetings between the two since 2022, with the home team winning in both Tuscaloosa and Knoxville. Both of those two Alabama losses in Knoxville have come in a pair of close games though, 52-49 and 24-17, both of which the Crimson Tide entered as the higher ranked team. Alabama struggled in multiple areas during both games, especially with penalties where they committed 17 and 15 in both, respectively. With the latest matchup also a Top 25 showdown similar to the previous two, can Alabama avoid a third-straight loss in Knoxville? away.headline: Georgia RB avoids injury scare after career game vs. Alabama
away.source: University of Georgia Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Phillips helped carry the Bulldogs to victory. He was a major contributor, making it difficult for Alabama defenders to bring him down. He had big plays that set up points for Georgia . Phillips did sustain what appeared to be an upper body injury, but he did return to the game in the third quarter. Undefeated Georgia will take on Auburn next on Saturday, Oct. 17. Phillips is not listed on SEC availability report. Bowens is listed as out while Frazier is not listed on the report, but he hasn't played recently and it would be surprising to see him play with Georgia's bye being the following week. The Georgia Bulldogs went against the Alabama Crimson Tide on Saturday, defeating them 20-17. Running back Dwight Phillips Jr. had a great performance, carrying the ball 17 times for 120 yards, averaging 7.1 yards per carry. "I feel a little beat up, but through six games I bet everyone is feeling a little bruised up,” Phillips said following the Alabama game. So far this season, Phillips has 255 yards and a touchdown. He's Georgia's leading rusher and one of the last Bulldogs left standing with Nate Frazier, Chauncey Bowens and Dante Dowdell all missing the Alabama game. Phillips' best game was against Alabama this past weekend. The run game is Georgia's bread and butter on offense, and they continue to lean on it. The Bulldogs have one of the best rushing attacks in the SEC. "This Dwight Phillips, man, y’all don’t know how special this kid is," Georgia coach Kirby Smart said on Phillips. "He ain’t complained one time since being here, and he’s so tough for his size." Follow UGA Wire on Instagram , Facebook , X (formerly Twitter) or Threads for more Georgia football coverage! away.headline: Alabama dealt unfortunate injury news ahead of Tennessee clash
away.blurb: The Alabama Crimson Tide will look to bounce back after a razor close loss to the Georgia Bulldogs in Week 6 when they face off against the Tennessee Volunteers. But unfortunately, they will not be at full strength offensively in Saturday’s game. Junior wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams has been one of the more reliable and effective wide receivers in all of college football this season for the Crimson Tide. Prior to their loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams had put together a three-game streak of finding the end zone at least once. During their Week 6 loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams was forced to exit the game after both seemingly re-aggravating a knee injury in the game and suffering a concussion, which was what ultimately cut his game in Week 6 short. More news : Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor Vows to ‘Ruin’ LSU’s Night Leading up to the team’s Week 7 game, there was not much optimism that Coleman-Williams was going to be able to suit up for the game. And that reality was confirmed on Wednesday when Alabama released their weekly injury report, along with a report on the matter from Pete Nakos of On3 Sports. More news : UCLA HC Bob Chesney Drops Powerful Quote After Bruins’ Hot Start Considering Coleman-Williams leads the team in every major statistical category, including receptions (tied with Lotzeir Brooks), receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns, his absence on Saturday will almost certainly be missed. Add in the fact that the Tennessee Volunteers allow just 161.3 passing yards per game to opposing teams, the second-lowest passing yards allowed to opponents in the SEC, and it could very well be a tough day for Alabama star quarterback Keelon Russell. Saturday’s Alabama-Tennessee matchup will kick off at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. away.headline: Alabama superstar ruled out of Tennessee game: See who will miss the matchup
away.blurb: Alabama football will be without one of its top playmakers for Saturday’s trip to Tennessee . Ryan Coleman-Williams was listed as out for the Third Saturday in October game, when the SEC released its first availability reporter for the matchup on Wednesday. With him out, Alabama will have to get more from some of its other receivers on Saturdays. Rico Scott, Derek Meadows, Noah Rogers and Cederian Morgan could all be in line for more snaps in Coleman-Williams’ absence. Coleman-Williams was one of six Alabama players listed as out. Desmond Umeozulu, Cayden Jones, Nick Sherman, Jeremiah Beaman and Terrance Green are also unavailable. Alabama starting center Racin Delgatty was listed as questionable. Delgatty left the loss to the Bulldogs late with a lower leg injury. Justin Hill appears to be nearing a return as well. The edge was listed as probable on Wednesday’s report. Ahead of the release, UA head coach Kalen DeBoer had foreshadowed Coleman-William’s absence for the game. “Right now we wouldn’t expect him to be with us as far as being on the field,” DeBoer said during his Wednesday radio show. “Going through a few different things, somf from games before, and one from the game on Saturday.” Coleman-Williams was wearing a brace on his right knee for the past two Alabama games. He left the Crimson TIde’s Saturday loss to Georgia looking extremely wobbly after a head-to-head hit that officials did not review for targeting, and DeBoer confirmed after the game the junior wideout had suffered a head injury. Green, a major contributor to the UA defensive line, left the Georgia game with an injury that DeBoer did not specify. DeBoer said he had reaggravated a previous issue. If Delgatty is unable to go, Crimson Tide offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb said that Mal Waldrep will get the nod at center. Waldrep, who battled for a starting guard spot this offseason before William Sanders won the job, took over snapping when Delgatty left the Georgia game. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit al.com. away.headline: Ryan Coleman-Williams ruled out for Alabama football vs Tennessee
away.blurb: The Alabama wide receiver is considered "week-to-week," per Crimson Tide coach Kalen DeBoer, with head and knee injuries. Coleman-Williams is listed as out on Alabama 's first SEC availability report Wednesday, Oct. 14, along with defensive linemen Jeremiah Beaman and Terrance Green, linebackers Cayden Jones and Desmond Umeozulu and defensive back Nick Sherman. Offensive lineman Racin Delgatty (lower leg) is questionable. Linebacker Justin Hill (lower body) is probable. DeBoer said Delgatty is limited in practice and is "pretty sore, kind of, working through things." Jorden Edmonds was a game-time decision before the Georgia game, but did not play against the Bulldogs. The five-star freshman has yet to make his Alabama debut and he is not listed on the availability report. Jones and Beaman are out for the season. Green re-aggravated a previous injury against Georgia. Hill has not played since Alabama's 50-36 win against Florida State on Sept. 19. He's been seen wearing a boot before the Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. Umeozulu has not played since Alabama's win against Florida State. He was seen wearing a boot and walking on crutches before the Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. Alabama kicks off against Tennessee at 2:30 p.m. CT Saturday, Oct. 17 on ABC. away.headline: Alabama Crimson Tide News: Injury worries cloud UT prep, secondary shakeup, SEC Tip-Off
away.blurb: Kalen DeBoer already said on Monday that it would be unlikely for star WR Ryan Coleman-Williams to be able to play. He's expected to be out , and the Crimson Tide will need guys like Noah Rogers, Derek Meadows, and Cederian Morgan to step up. Starting defensive tackle Terrance Green's status is up in the air, too. Green left the game against Georgia late in the first half and didn't return. There was a noticeable difference between the Crimson Tide's run defense with Green and without him. Alabama has been hoping sophomore CB Dijon Lee could fight through his poor performance on the field early in the season and come out the other side a better player. They've been willing to roll with him because his potential is sky-high. With Ryan Coleman-Williams likely out at Tennessee, opportunity knocks for Noah Rogers Alabama Crimson Tide news and notes: Alabama could be down three starters at Tennessee this weekend Clarity should come this evening when the SEC releases this week's availability reports, but there's concern for Alabama with three key starters ahead of this weekend's matchup in Knoxville. There's concern about starting center Racin Delgatty, too, who went down with an injury on Alabama's last offensive snap against Georgia. He has a lower extremity issue, but his status is currently unknown. If he's unable to go, sophomore Mal Waldrep is expected to start in his place. In a game Alabama really needs to win following last week's loss to Georgia, it could have to navigate the tricky road trip without three more key players. Kane Wommack could shake things up at CB following Dijon Lee's meltdown vs. Georgia But last week against Georgia, he paired struggles in coverage with a massive mental mistake late in the game that cost the Crimson Tide a chance to get the ball back. It led to a public butt-chewing from DeBoer and now has Kane Wommack clearly considering a chance at corner. "The things that I need to do to get him to execute at a higher level than what he’s doing, from an execution standpoint, that’s one facet. And then the other facet is being held accountable for the penalty there at the end of the game. There will be some things that we will do this week, and some things that moving forward - my job as a coordinator is based on the production that you put on the field, the role that you have moving forward. From a rep-based standpoint, that will be reflected in what guys have done to this point.” Alabama basketball picked to finish 5th in SEC preseason poll Nate Oats and Alabama basketball were picked to finish 5th in the preseason SEC poll. That's a good omen for the program. In the two seasons in which Oats led the Crimson Tide to SEC regular-season and tournament titles (2020-21 and 2022-23), Alabama was picked in the preseason to finish fifth in the league. home.blurb: Brandon was listed on the SEC availability report as questionable throughout the week and then as a game-time decision on the final availability report on game day. "George handled it well when Faizon got named the starter, and Faizon's handled it well dealing with his shoulder, continuing to stay invested at practice, in the meeting room, helping that room out," Heupel said. "(He) was here for emergency use only this week." Sophomore George MacIntyre made his first career start, leading Tennessee to a 24-17 victory over Arkansas. Coach Josh Heupel stated the decision to start MacIntyre was made early in the week. Heupel indicated the team will "play it by ear" regarding the starting quarterback position moving forward. Tennessee football coach Josh Heupel revealed that the decision about the Vols' starting quarterback for Arkansas was made at the beginning of the week, but they're going to "play it by ear" going forward. Sophomore George MacIntyre got his first career start and led the No. 14 Vols to a 24-17 win over Arkansas on Oct. 10 in their first SEC road game. MacIntyre finished the Auburn game on Oct. 3 after freshman Faizon Brandon was benched during the second quarter. Brandon is dealing with a right shoulder injury, which he suffered during the 20-17 loss to Texas on Sept. 26. "Just with what he was dealing with, (Brandon) really didn't rep during the course of the week," Heupel said after the Arlansas win. "George knew on Monday that he was going to start this week, and we'll continue to play it by ear as we keep going. The strength of one room can never be one guy. I know most of you guys are tired of me saying that, but that's the truth of it. And we'll keep growing and going." When asked how Brandon has dealt with being benched as a young quarterback, Heupel repeated that he's "dealing with an injury." Brandon was named Tennessee's starter as a true freshman to start the 2026 season. The 6-foot-4, 225-pounder has completed 61 of 101 passes this season for 697 yards, seven touchdowns and one interception. Brandon has also rushed for 130 yards on 53 carries for three touchdowns.

Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. Ole Miss vs. Missouri Preview: Rebels Face Tough Test Against Rising Tigers
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Missouri Preview: Rebels Face Tough Test Against Rising Tigers - SEC Country Skip to content Alabama Mississippi State South Carolina Instagram X-twitter Youtube Search Search Shop Alabama Stephan Stroud October 14, 2026 No. 9 Ole Miss will host No. 13 Missouri on Saturday afternoon in a major SEC matchup featuring two teams looking to strengthen their position in the conference race. The Rebels enter the game at 4-1 overall and 2-1 in SEC play after dominating Vanderbilt 52-17 last weekend. Missouri arrives in Oxford at 5-1 overall and 2-1 in conference action following an impressive 27-6 victory over Texas A&M. Kickoff is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. CT at Vaught Hemingway Stadium, with the game airing on the SEC Network. With both teams ranked inside the top 15, Saturday’s matchup could be one of the most important games of the weekend. Trinidad Chambliss Leads Ole Miss Ole Miss will once again turn to quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who has become the key part of the Rebels’ offense. Latest episode SEC Country Podcast New shows Monday & Wednesday Airing It Out with Aaron Murray · Sep 25 The Rebels have shown that they can create explosive plays through the air, and Chambliss has played an important role in keeping the offense productive. Ole Miss will need another efficient performance from its quarterback against a Missouri defense that has been particularly strong against the run. The Tigers are allowing just 78.3 rushing yards per game, making it important for Chambliss to take advantage of opportunities in the passing game. Golding, who took over as Ole Miss head coach, will also want his offense to maintain the physicality and consistency it showed against Vanderbilt. Austin Simmons Returns to Oxford One of the biggest storylines will be Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons returning to face his former team . Simmons previously played for Ole Miss before transferring to Missouri, where he has become the leader of the Tigers’ offense. Through five games, Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards and 14 touchdowns. He has shown impressive arm talent and the ability to make plays outside the pocket, giving Missouri a quarterback capable of challenging opposing defenses in multiple ways. Simmons completed 14 of 28 passes for 147 yards and a touchdown against Texas A&M, helping Missouri secure a 27-6 victory. Although the passing numbers were not overwhelming, the Tigers controlled the game and delivered one of their strongest defensive performances of the season. Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz will look for Simmons to be more efficient against an Ole Miss team that knows his strengths and weaknesses. The familiarity between Simmons and his former teammates adds another layer to an already intriguing matchup. Eli Drinkwitz Has Missouri Rolling Drinkwitz has Missouri positioned for another important season in the SEC. The Tigers have combined a productive offense with a defense that has consistently made life difficult for opponents. Missouri is averaging 35.8 points per game while allowing just 17.7 points per contest. Running back Jamal Rogers has also become a major part of the Tigers’ success, leading the SEC with 828 rushing yards entering the matchup. His ability to control the ground game could be especially important against an Ole Miss defense that has struggled to stop the run at times this season. The Tigers will look to establish Rogers early, allowing Simmons to work from manageable passing situations. A Major SEC Opportunity Ole Miss and Missouri both enter Saturday with plenty to prove. The Rebels want to build on their victory over Vanderbilt and demonstrate that they can compete consistently against ranked SEC opponents. Missouri hopes to continue its strong start and earn another important conference victory on the road. The quarterback matchup between Chambliss and Simmons will be central to the outcome, while the coaching battle between Golding and Drinkwitz adds another compelling storyline. With Missouri’s rushing attack facing an Ole Miss defense that needs to remain disciplined, and the Rebels looking to exploit opportunities through the air, both teams will have important challenges to solve. Saturday’s showdown in Oxford gives Ole Miss a chance to protect its home field, while Missouri arrives looking to prove its 5-1 start is no fluke. Missouri is 5-1 overall and 2-1 in SEC play after beating Texas A&M 27-6 on Oct. 10. Ole Miss is 4-1 overall and 2-1 in conference games following a 52-17 rout of Vanderbilt the same day. Both teams climbed in the polls this week, with Missouri moving to No. 13 in the AP Top 25 and Coaches Poll and Ole Miss sitting at No. 9 in the AP poll and No. 10 in the Coaches Poll, according to 247Sports . Missouri Vs Ole Miss Preview: Game Information Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 3:30 p.m. ET Venue: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford, Mississippi TV: SEC Network What Does The Austin Simmons Return Mean? Simmons started at Ole Miss before losing his job to Trinidad Chambliss following a Week 3 injury last season, and he never started another game for the Rebels, according to CBS Sports . Chambliss went on to throw for 3,937 yards, finish eighth in Heisman voting and lead Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff semifinals. Simmons entered the transfer portal after that playoff run and landed at Missouri, where he has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns and just one interception this season while completing 64.8% of his passes. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding addressed facing his former backup turned starter elsewhere. “It's scary to know how good he is and how talented he is,” Golding said, per CBS Sports. Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz praised how Simmons handled the demotion before his move. “I think the biggest thing is he's a tremendous teammate. He showed great leadership. You go from being the starting quarterback to getting Wally Pipped and now you're having to be the encourager,” Drinkwitz said. Simmons has not downplayed the difficulty of the exit. “It was tough leaving. I'd been there for so long,” he said at Missouri's preseason media day in August. Chambliss, for his part, called the setup unusual. “Going to be weird to see them in different colors,” he said after Ole Miss' win at Vanderbilt. Who Else Made The Jump From Oxford To Columbia? Simmons is not the only player who left Ole Miss for Missouri. Wide receiver Cayden Lee, who played three seasons with the Rebels, has caught 41 passes for 616 yards and five touchdowns through six games at Missouri. Cornerback Chris Graves Jr. also made the transfer. Simmons has been named SEC Offensive Player of the Week twice this season, according to Sports Illustrated . How Have Both Teams Trended Since Their Only Loss? Ole Miss' lone defeat came 52-28 at Florida on Sept. 26, a game in which Gators running back Jadan Baugh ran 29 times for 142 yards and three touchdowns. Missouri later beat that same Florida team 45-17, with Baugh limited to 12 carries for 13 yards, a swing Sports Illustrated flagged as a point of comparison between the two SEC contenders. Missouri's only loss this season came on the road against Mississippi State, three weeks before its 27-6 win over Texas A&M. Since that setback, the Tigers have won two straight, including a 45-17 win over Florida the week before facing the Aggies. What Do The Season Numbers Say About Each Offense? Ole Miss ranks among the most efficient scoring offenses in the country, leading the FBS by converting 100% of its red zone trips into points. The Rebels average 439.0 passing yards per game, 39th nationally, and 302.7 rushing yards per game, 29th nationally, for a total of 392.4 yards per game that ranks 108th in the FBS. Missouri averages 433.8 total yards per game, 43rd nationally. Turnovers mark a clear separation point. Missouri ranks 15th in the FBS with a plus-5 turnover margin, while Ole Miss sits 77th at minus-1. Missouri also controls the clock better, averaging 30 minutes 30 seconds of possession per game (59th nationally) compared to Ole Miss's 26:08 average, which ranks 135th. On defense, Ole Miss has struggled on third down, ranking 123rd nationally by allowing a 45.9% conversion rate, while Missouri's offense converts 42.7% of its own third-down chances, good for 57th in the FBS. By the Numbers Total offense per game: Missouri 433.8 yards, Ole Miss 392.4 yards Passing yards per game: Missouri 256.5, Ole Miss 300.6 Rushing yards per game: Missouri 181.7, Ole Miss 133.2 Points per game: Missouri 35.8, Ole Miss 38.8 Turnover margin: Missouri +1, Ole Miss 0 Third-down conversion rate: Missouri 42.17%, Ole Miss 43.10% Time of possession: Missouri 10,686 seconds total, Ole Miss 7,766 seconds total Total takeaways: Missouri 4, Ole Miss 7 Missouri Outlook Quarterback Austin Simmons has completed 107 of 165 passes for 1,434 yards with 14 touchdowns against a single interception this season. Running back Jamal Roberts has carried the load on the ground with 828 yards and eight touchdowns on 147 attempts, and he posted 222 yards and two touchdowns on 34 carries in the win over Texas A&M. Receiver Cayden Lee has caught 42 passes for 616 yards and five scores. Missouri's plus-5 turnover margin and 30:30 average time of possession reflect a ball-control approach that has produced wins in four of its last five games, with the only blemish coming at Mississippi State. Ole Miss Outlook Trinidad Chambliss has thrown for 1,435 yards with 11 touchdowns and four interceptions on 70.1% completion this season, and he added 213 yards, three touchdowns and one interception through the air plus a rushing score in the win over Vanderbilt. Running back Kewan Lacy has totaled 230 yards and five touchdowns on just 46 carries, while receiver Deuce Alexander has 503 yards and five touchdowns on 32 catches, including a five-catch, 74-yard, one-touchdown performance against Vanderbilt. Ole Miss' red zone offense leads the FBS at a 100% scoring rate, but the Rebels' minus-1 turnover margin and 123rd-ranked third-down defense are areas Missouri's offense could look to exploit. What To Watch Ole Miss has won 14 consecutive games at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium dating back to late September 2024, a home streak Missouri will try to end on the road. Both teams remain in the thick of the SEC race at 2-1 in conference play, and a win would strengthen either program's playoff positioning given their rankings in the AP Top 25 and Coaches Poll. Ole Miss turns around quickly to face No. 7 Texas on Oct. 24, while Missouri heads to Arkansas on Oct. 31. More College Football news from Total Apex Sports. away.headline: Missouri's extensive injury report is looking increasingly like a nothingburger
away.blurb: The injury reports for Texas A&M and Missouri could not have looked more different coming into their huge game this morning, but it's looking more and more like that was all for show. The Aggies were down Terry Bussey (who is out for the season) and Blake Ivy, with Mario Craver listed as questionable, but it was the laundry list of players on Missouri's side that caught the eye of fans. The Tigers had listed as questionable players like star OL Cayden Green, starting S Santana Banner, and star Auburn transfer LB Robert Woodyard— in all, three of their top four tacklers on defense, as well as a remarkable number of offensive weapons. However, as game time has drawn nearer this morning, it looks like all of the hubbub around Missouri's potential missing players is possibly for naught. Reporting is emerging that some of the big time players for the Tigers that were listed as questionable in this game are on track to play, showing that the Aggies will indeed be facing a Mizzou team at nearly-full strength this week. Pete Thamel of ESPN reports that the Tigers' starting edge defenders, Darris Smith and Langden Kitchen, will both be playing against A&M in this game as well; both had been listed as questionable coming into the game. The game day update of the injury report confirms this from Thamel and Zenitz, as every single player that was listed as questionable or probable for the Tigers has been removed from the list , apparently set to play in this one. That's not only dismaying for the Aggies, it's a bit questionable on the part of the Tigers. We saw some interesting usage of the report by Lane Kiffin earlier this season, and though Eli Drinkwitz likes to do a bit of trolling from time to time, he doesn't quite have the same reputation as the LSU head coach does. While that's not an accusation that he was definitively misusing the report, it is odd that not a single player of the seven listed on the report as questionable actually will end up being unavailable for this game. That said, though, just because a player is not listed as "out" on this report does not mean that they are a sure thing to play in the game: we saw that with Jamarion Morrow last week for the Aggies. Texas A&M's optimism suddenly tamped down as Missouri's injury report apparently set to shrink Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports that Green, Banner, and Woodyard are all set to play in this game, which will be a huge relief for Tiger fans— but grim news for the Aggies, who definitely need all the help they can get in this one. In all, though, this means that Texas A&M will indeed have a challenge ahead of them today of a Tigers team at almost full strength. The Aggies need this win, but it was never going to come easy— this development only underlines that fact. away.headline: Ole Miss defensive back Edwin Joseph ruled out against Missouri after ankle surgery
away.blurb: This isn't quite a worst-case scenario for Ole Miss, but it's not far down the list either. The Rebels will be without starting defensive back Edwin Joseph on Saturday against No. 13 Missouri after he underwent a tightrope procedure Wednesday to repair the high ankle sprain he suffered in last week's 52-17 win at Vanderbilt. Joseph was officially ruled out on the SEC's availability report Wednesday night , though Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding had already hinted earlier in the week that the injury was serious enough to warrant concern. Joseph traveled to Birmingham on Tuesday for a second medical opinion before undergoing surgery on his left ankle . The expected recovery timeline is 10-14 days, which means Saturday's game is obviously off the table and next week's trip to Texas could be in doubt as well. The good news, if there is any, is that tightrope procedures typically come with shorter recovery timelines than some traditional ankle surgeries. The bad news is Ole Miss is losing one of its most reliable defensive backs at a time when the secondary had finally started to look settled. Joseph, a senior transfer from Florida State, opened the season at safety before spending much of the last several weeks at cornerback. Wherever Ole Miss needed him, he played. Through five games, he's totaled 18 tackles and a pass breakup while providing versatility that allowed the Rebels to move pieces around the secondary. That's what makes this loss sting. Ole Miss is not losing just a starter. It's losing one of the defensive backs who had emerged as a stabilizing presence in a group that has dealt with position shuffling for much of the season. His absence comes on the heels of arguably the defense's best performance of the year at Vanderbilt, when the Rebels forced four turnovers and looked far more aggressive and disruptive than they had in previous weeks. Now they'll have to maintain that momentum without one of their most experienced players on the back end.
