home.headline: Ole Miss defensive back Edwin Joseph ruled out against Missouri after ankle surgery
home.blurb: This isn't quite a worst-case scenario for Ole Miss, but it's not far down the list either. The Rebels will be without starting defensive back Edwin Joseph on Saturday against No. 13 Missouri after he underwent a tightrope procedure Wednesday to repair the high ankle sprain he suffered in last week's 52-17 win at Vanderbilt. Joseph was officially ruled out on the SEC's availability report Wednesday night , though Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding had already hinted earlier in the week that the injury was serious enough to warrant concern. Joseph traveled to Birmingham on Tuesday for a second medical opinion before undergoing surgery on his left ankle . The expected recovery timeline is 10-14 days, which means Saturday's game is obviously off the table and next week's trip to Texas could be in doubt as well. The good news, if there is any, is that tightrope procedures typically come with shorter recovery timelines than some traditional ankle surgeries. The bad news is Ole Miss is losing one of its most reliable defensive backs at a time when the secondary had finally started to look settled. Joseph, a senior transfer from Florida State, opened the season at safety before spending much of the last several weeks at cornerback. Wherever Ole Miss needed him, he played. Through five games, he's totaled 18 tackles and a pass breakup while providing versatility that allowed the Rebels to move pieces around the secondary. That's what makes this loss sting. Ole Miss is not losing just a starter. It's losing one of the defensive backs who had emerged as a stabilizing presence in a group that has dealt with position shuffling for much of the season. His absence comes on the heels of arguably the defense's best performance of the year at Vanderbilt, when the Rebels forced four turnovers and looked far more aggressive and disruptive than they had in previous weeks. Now they'll have to maintain that momentum without one of their most experienced players on the back end. The Hurricanes have been particularly effective limiting opponents and forcing opposing offenses into uncomfortable situations. Florida State needs to establish its rushing attack while avoiding turnovers that provide Miami with favorable field position. The Seminoles also have to overcome their road struggles, having now lost 13 consecutive games away from home. away.headline: Initial week 7 injury report for Florida State vs. No. 3 Miami could spell disaster for the Seminoles
away.blurb: Florida State needs some luck on its side to take down Miami, but that might not happen with multiple players notably absent from the initial injury report . The Hurricanes had two starters in particular suffer injuries last time out against Clemson, but neither player was included in the injury report, which means the Seminoles will be getting the best version of Miami in Week 7. DB Romanas Frederique Jr. (out) LB Noah LaVallee (questionable) No Lightfoot and no McCoy on the injury report likely means Florida State will be playing against a full-strength Miami team. The Hurricanes have a few players who have been ruled out for the game, but nothing serious has changed from last week. That could be an issue for the Seminoles, who already will face two serious mismatches in Week 7. The Hurricanes' offense could also receive a boost if McCoy avoids having to sit out the Week 7 game against the Seminoles. There is no two ways about it, Florida State has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season. The performance against Virginia in Week 5 was exceptional, but it should be viewed as the outlier at this point, with more disappointing performances than positive ones on defense. Florida State is just days away from perhaps the biggest game on the schedule against ACC rivals No. 3 Miami. The Hurricanes have displayed arguably the best offense and the best defense in the country this season, while the Seminoles have struggled to play consistent football. Starting edge rusher and Miami's sack leader, Marquise Lightfoot, left the game against Clemson early, but the star defender was not included in the first Week 7 injury report. Additionally, starting right tackle Matthew McCoy was attended to by the training staff against the Tigers, but ultimately played the rest of the game. McCoy was also not included in the initial Week 7 injury report for Miami. Marquise Lightfoot, Matthew McCoy left off Miami's initial injury report for the Florida State game For Miami, getting Lightfoot back would be tremendous due to how quickly he can create an impact on the field. Lightfoot disrupts offenses, and Florida State's best chance at igniting the offense is by giving the football to dynamic running back Ousmane Kromah. The running back has been the one constant this season for the Seminoles' offense, but he may meet his match against Lightfoot. Lightfoot currently has 20 total tackles and five sacks this season, with a sack in each of his last four games. The defender also recorded a sack and two tackles against Clemson before exiting, and while Miami has a lot of talent capable of filling the potential void, nobody creates quite as much chaos as Lightfoot does. It is going to be very hard for Florida State, a team that already struggles with generating pressure, to do so against a team like Miami, who have only allowed five total sacks this season. The Seminoles cannot win this game if quarterback Darian Mensah is given a clean pock

picks.headline: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling
picks.blurb: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 15, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Following an emotional win vs. No. 10 LSU, Kentucky heads to Oklahoma to face a Sooners team that just beat No. 1 Texas. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners’ running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 5-1 under first-year head coach Will Stein after a huge upset over LSU, while Oklahoma is coming off a rivalry win over Texas. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. Despite concerns about linebacker injuries, the Wildcats have a chance to improve to 6-1, become bowl-eligible, and remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. picks.headline: How No. 15 Kentucky football & Oklahoma match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Having led Kentucky to back-to-back 35-34 overtime wins, Kenny Minchey is proving himself a cool customer under game-deciding stress. Two weeks ago at South Carolina, Minchey had running back CJ Baxter make a pre-snap shift so he could pick up an otherwise-free edge rusher. As the block was achieved, Minchey threw the game-winning two-point-conversion pass. Last week, Minchey realized the LSU defense had a Grand Canyon-sized hole in the middle of its formation. On a called pass play, the Hendersonville, Tennessee, product instead ran right through that hole for the game-winning two-point-conversion run. On the season, the 6-foot-2, 211-pound Minchey is completing 67.4% of his passes and has thrown for 1,394 yards with 11 touchdown throws vs. one interception. • Oklahoma’s John Mateer began the season on the outskirts of the Heisman Trophy discussion but has so far had a rough go in 2026. Ball security has been a problem for the 6-1, 224-pound Mateer. He threw a crucial interception late in Oklahoma’s 17-10 loss at Michigan in Week 2. He also turned the ball over three times in the first half at Georgia on Sept. 26, helping the Bulldogs open a 28-0 halftime lead en route to a 41-13 win. In Oklahoma’s 27-24 upset of then-No. 1 Texas last week, however, Mateer completed 18 of 26 passes for 155 yards with no interceptions. Mateer has not been as effective a rusher so far in 2026 as he has been in past seasons. Through five games, Mateer has a net-70 yards rushing. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky’s CJ Baxter ripped off a 77-yard run on UK’s first play from scrimmage in last week’s win over LSU. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, finished with 123 rushing yards on 19 carries against the Tigers. A transfer from Texas, Baxter is fifth in the SEC in rushing with 484 yards. Third-year player Jason Patterson has carried only seven times combined in the past two games after suffering an apparent injury at South Carolina. A 5-10, 204-pound product of Sneads, Florida, Patterson had been one of UK’s breakout players over the season’s first four games. • Oklahoma’s ground game has, so far, been mostly stalled. The Sooners are last in the SEC in rushing, averaging only 95.8 yards a game. Lloyd Avant Jr ., a transfer from Colorado State who began his college career at Tulsa, leads the Sooners in rushing with 239 yards and two touchdowns on 52 carries (an average of 4.5 yards a rush). Avant, however, had a strong showing in the win over Texas, rushing 10 times for 72 yards and a touchdown. Wide receivers • Kentucky true freshman Kenny Darby was named SEC Freshman of the Week for the second straight week after catching four passes for 79 yards, including two crucial receptions late in the game, in the win over LSU. On the season, Darby, a 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, is eighth in the SEC in receptions (29) and ninth in receiving yards (401). Ja’Kayden Ferguson had caught only three total passes in UK’s first five games, but the 6-2, 184-pound, second-year player made three key receptions in the win over LSU. “He made some unbelievable plays,” Will Stein said of Ferguson. “... He blocked hard. He played hard. He’s got a lot of talent, a lot of upside.” • Isaiah Sategna III has been Oklahoma’s most effective offensive skill player so far in 2026. The 5-10, 185-pound senior from Austin, Texas, has 25 catches for 331 yards and two touchdowns. Sategna caught five passes for 64 yards in the win over Texas. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez made a team-high six catches for 25 yards vs. LSU. A 6-4, 249-pound junior from Covington Catholic, Rodriguez is second on the UK team in receptions (28) and receiving yards (219). Henry Boyer had a quiet showing vs. LSU with one catch for four yards. The 6-6, 270-pound transfer from Illinois has only nine catches on the season, but those receptions have yielded 120 receiving yards and three touchdowns. • Oklahoma’s Rocky Beers is, like UK’s Rodriguez, one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the SEC. A 6-5, 240-pound senior from Littleton, Colorado, Beers has 22 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Beers had four catches for 29 yards vs. Texas. Hayden Hansen caught 30 passes for 254 yards and two TDs last season while playing for Florida. So far this season, the 6-8, 270-pound Hansen has five catches for 74 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even Offensive line • After having a rough go against Alabama in Week 2, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has consistently been playing solid football. “Malachi is a really-good football player,” Will Stein said. “The guy is 6-8, 330 pounds. He is gonna be, probably, a top three-round NFL draft pick in the next couple years. “ • The Oklahoma offensive front has been much-criticized amidst the Sooners’ offensive struggles, but the unit showed some signs of hope in the second half vs. Texas. Freshman Noah Best has emerged as the jack-of-all-trades on the OU offensive line, already logging starts this season at center and both guard positions. Defensive line • Kentucky nose guard Jamarrion Harkless was one of the unsung heroes of the win over LSU. The 6-3, 346-pound alumnus of Frederick Douglass High School made three tackles, 1.5 sacks, forced a fumble and had a quarterback hurry against Lane Kiffin’s Tigers. “I told (Harkless) ‘That’s how you have to play for us to be successful on defense, game in, game out,’” Will Stein said. • Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone is an interior force. The 6-3, 312-pound junior from Del City, Oklahoma, made five tackles in the win over Texas. On the season, Stone has 19 tackles, two tackles for loss and half a sack. Advantage : Oklahoma • Due to injuries, Kentucky starting linebackers Grant Godfrey and Bo Barnes had to be iron men vs. LSU. WLB Barnes made 12 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss, while MLB Godfrey made 10 stops vs. the Tigers. • Oklahoma MLB Owen Heinecke leads the Sooners in tackles (36), is tied for the team lead in quarterback hurries (two) and is second in tackles for loss (4.5). A 6-1, 226-pound fifth-year player from Tulsa, Heinecke made nine tackles vs. Texas. Defensive backs • Kentucky senior strong safety Ty Bryant made six tackles and intercepted a pass vs. LSU. For the 6-foot, 196-pound Bryant, a product of Frederick Douglass High School, it was his sixth career pick. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols made seven tackles and successfully defended a pass vs. LSU. • Oklahoma strong safety Peyton Bowen returned an interception of Texas quarterback Arch Manning 42 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter last week. A 6-foot, 200-pound product of Corinth, Texas, Bowen has made 24 tackles on the season, leads the Sooners in pass breakups with four and also has a forced fumble and a sack. Special teams • Kentucky punt returner Brock Coffman brought an LSU kick back 55 yards for a touchdown last week. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui entered last week’s game 6 of 7 on field-goal attempts but went only 2 of 4 vs. LSU. However, after missing two makeable field goals in the fourth quarter last week, Zouagui came back to hit a 33-yard field goal with 12 seconds left in the contest to tie the game at 27 and force overtime. picks.blurb: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Kentucky Wildcats final score predictions: Can the Sooners get back in the CFP discussion with a win? Skip to content NFL Close Menu All NFL Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks College Football Close Menu All College Football Alabama Crimson Tide Auburn Tigers Florida Gators Georgia Bulldogs Miami Hurricanes Michigan Wolverines Notre Dame Fighting Irish Ohio State Buckeyes Oklahoma Sooners Ole Miss Rebels Penn State Nittany Lions Tennessee Volunteers Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Draft Simulator Trade Simulator Toggle Mobile Navigation Home College Football The Oklahoma Sooners will host a strong Kentucky Wildcats team on Saturday night. The Oklahoma Sooners are coming off of a huge win over the Texas Longhorns at the Cotton Bowl in the Red River Rivalry. The Kentucky Wildcats are coming off a huge overtime win over LSU. Both teams are on a high but are looking to improve their records on Saturday night. So, does the team in Kentucky that's maybe at its best as a program get the win? Or does Oklahoma get another ranked win and get back into the College Football Playoff conversation? Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Oklahoma 20, Kentucky 17 This feels almost like the clock striking midnight for Kentucky here, as much as it does for me, who's lived the last two weeks dangerously. Both teams are coming in off super highs from last week. Oklahoma clipped Texas 27-24 on a walk-off field goal. Kentucky walked off LSU 35-34 in overtime, their second straight walk-off overtime win, going for two and getting it on the final play. Honestly, in a vacuum, I trust Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey more than I trust OU's John Mateer. But Minchey is going up against a very good Oklahoma defense, while Mateer has a more navigable task when he has the ball. I still don't see points a plenty here, but Oklahoma forces a key turnover late, and that's enough with the home crowd in Norman to get a close and resume-boosting win at the season's midpoint. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 20 This could be one of the ugliest games on the schedule, with both teams struggling to find much offensive consistency. Oklahoma will have chances to pull away, but John Mateer’s chaotic style makes it hard to trust the Sooners to put together four clean quarters. Mateer can make spectacular plays, but mistakes and questionable decisions could give Kentucky the extra possessions it needs to hang around. Don't expect a shootout here. This game could come down to which team makes fewer costly mistakes in the fourth quarter. I'm buying a little bit of Kentucky magic in this one. Kenny Minchey comes through with a couple of clutch plays at the biggest moments, giving the Wildcats just enough offense to pull off a road upset. Kentucky might not look dominant, and it certainly won't be pretty, but this team finds a way to make things interesting when the game is on the line. Oklahoma has a chance to put the Wildcats away but can't quite finish the job, opening the door for Kentucky to steal a win in a close, low-scoring battle. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 16 Will Stein has the Wildcats on a heater right now, and he's doing it with the two things you want in Kentucky's place: confidence and guts. He's won two games this season because the Wildcats went for two at the end, and that kind of belief in your team will go a long way in establishing a foundation for your program. Things are different for the Sooners, who are coming off of a fantastic win in Red River. Even so, John Mateer can't do much other than throw shock, and he did that brilliantly on the final drive against Texas. I don't think Mateer will change overnight, and the Wildcats will take advantage of him enough to win. Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 14 This game suddenly looks much better than it did a week ago after both Kentucky and Oklahoma pulled off massive upsets last weekend. Red River can always get wonky, but few expected OU to beat the number one team in the nation given how the offense has played. Will Stein's Wildcats have gone from quietly looking like a good football team to potentially being one of the conference's better teams after just one loss to Alabama and a last-minute OT win over LSU. The truth, however, is that OU may have found something more than just some Red River magic. This will be arguably the hardest test of the year for Kenny Minchey, and the battle of the brains between Brent Venables and Will Stein will be notable, but I think Oklahoma will get the job done. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 17 The Oklahoma Sooners are almost ready to kick off their first SEC night game (excluding CFP games) since 2024. And this one should be big, with both teams riding an insane high after huge wins. The Kentucky Wildcats will give OU's defense fits. It will happen, and I know my score prediction probably doesn't show that, but I have OU getting a few takeaways in this one. Kentucky is going to do a bunch of pre-snap stuff that's going to confuse you. They are very good at that, but Brent Venables has his unit locked in right now. OU will win this game once again through the defense and special teams, with some little moments here and there from the offense. home.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky: Initial Week 7 Availability Report
home.blurb: Fasusi has missed each of Oklahoma's last four games after playing in a limited role in the season opener against the UTEP Miners. Head coach Brent Venables said he was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Along with Fasusi, offensive linemen Eddy Pierre-Louis and Heath Ozaeta were also listed as questionable. Both players started games for the Sooners this season. Ozaeta played against Texas despite limping off the field during warm-ups. Pierre-Louis missed the Texas game and was on crutches during the pre-game coin toss and on the sideline. Wide receiver Parker Livingstone is the only other questionable name on the injury report. Livingstone started against Texas and played 29 snaps, but didn't register a target in the game. He hasn't really produced much since coming over from Texas in the transfer portal. Livingstone has six receptions for 51 yards this season. If Fasusi, Pierre-Louis, and Ozaeta all miss the Kentucky game, the Sooners will need a new right-guard starter, likely Peyton Joseph. Cornerback Eli Bowen is a key name to watch for the Sooners' defense. He was injured in practice on Thursday and missed the win over Texas. If he doesn't play Saturday night, Trystan Haynes would get his second consecutive start after playing well against the Longhorns . For the Kentucky Wildcats, one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). home.headline: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma Injury Report: Updates on CJ Baxter, Nic Anderson, and more
home.blurb: For Kentucky, the big news is that running back CJ Baxter is questionable to play this week. Baxter got dinged in the second half of the win over LSU but still finished the game and ran for a touchdown in overtime. He’s been one of the SEC’s best backs thus far, so not having him in Norman would be a major setback for this offense. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, who left last week’s win over LSU with a shoulder injury, is listed as probable, so he should be good to go this week as long as there are no setbacks. Defensive tackle Kalen Edwards, who missed last week, is questionable to play. As expected, linebacker Antwan Smith and cornerback Jaden Smith remain out after suffering injuries at South Carolina. Linebacker Tavion Wallace, out for the past two weeks, is still listed as out. Fellow linebacker Alex Afari Jr. is listed as questionable as he works through the legal process in hopes of regaining eligibility. He’s healthy, so if granted eligibility in the courts, he should play Saturday, but that’s a big if right now. Cornerback Grant Grayton remains out. Reserve defensive end Tyler Thomas is doubtful. Reserve tight end Elijah Brown is questionable. Finally, cornerback Hassan Sykes is probable to play. For Oklahoma, standout left tackle Michael Fasusi is nearing a return from a shoulder injury that has kept him out since Week 1. He’s currently listed as questionable. Starting left guard Eddy Pierre-Louis, who missed last week’s win over No. 1 Texas, is questionable. Backup lineman Fred Hinton is questionable as well. Cornerback Eli Bowen, who missed last week, is questionable to play. Fellow cornerback Jacobe Johnson, who was also out last week, is listed as out for this one. Wide receiver Parker Livingstone, who has six catches for 51 yards this year, is questionable. Running back Tory Blaylock, who has 10 carries for 22 yards, is probable. Tight end Jack Van Dorselaer, who does not have a catch this season, is probable. Finally, linebacker Taylor Heim, running back Xavier Robinson, tight end Trynae Washington, and wide receiver Trell Harris have been ruled out. home.blurb: Nic Anderson left LSU win with injury just days before his return to Oklahoma | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 15, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Kentucky Wildcats wide receiver Nic Anderson left Saturday night’s 35-34 overtime win over the No. 10 LSU Tigers in the second half and did not return. UK radio’s Dick Gabriel reported during the game that Anderson was being evaluated for a shoulder injury and was questionable to return, though the fifth-year senior never came back. There’s no official word yet on how serious it is. Stein will likely give an update at his Tuesday press conference. Through his first four games as a Wildcat, Anderson had four catches for 40 yards. Then he went to Columbia and broke out with five catches for 80 yards and his first touchdown in Kentucky blue in the 35-34 overtime win at South Carolina. That game also pushed him past 1,000 career receiving yards. It was his first touchdown since September 2025. If Anderson can’t go, this would be a familiar and frustrating chapter for him. A quad injury limited him to one game at Oklahoma in 2024. At LSU, he was hurt in a car accident the summer before the season and then suffered a knee injury against Alabama in November that ended his year. Kentucky handled him carefully all offseason, holding him out of the spring game and the start of fall camp, and it had been paying off. Barnes’ quick return was a relief for a linebacker room Stein called thin heading into the game. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! picks.headline: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon
picks.blurb: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule knows 55 minutes of good football isn't enough. It might be against some teams, but not most. As the Huskers look to bounce back from a three-point loss to defending national champion Indiana , Rhule and his staff are making that a point of emphasis for the entire team. At the same time, Rhule is willing to bet on his quarterback to get the job done. Meeting with the media Monday, Rhule reiterated that message and shed light on the Big Red's preparations for its Week 7 road game against the Oregon Ducks. Here's everything he had to say. Anthony Colandrea looks to pass against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. Asked about going for it on fourth-and-nine, the head coach pointed to what the analytics said: Go for it. It didn't work out this time, but he said he'd do it again. “I just felt like I was going to follow the analytics and put the ball in Anthony’s hands,” Rhule said. “We had holes that we thought were open and felt like, if we wanted to win that game, that ball and that field position, when you needed about 20 yards to kick a field goal, I’m going to put it in Colandrea's hands.” “I don’t always follow the analytics,” he continued. “I felt like our defense would get the stop, but more importantly, I just felt like I needed to put this ball in my guys' hands. I will ride or die with Anthony Colandrea all day, every day.” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti and FOX Sports' Joel Klatt walk on the sideline during warmups before Saturday's game. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. Rhule knows the Huskers need to be better in a few key moments, like that fourth-and-nine, but he doesn't believe the team needs to overhaul much. “When we watched the tape on Sunday, I think you have a team that is angry, who knows they let one get away,” he said. “We’re certainly disappointed, but not discouraged. We also understand that that is what it looks like. You have to not play really well for 55 minutes, you have to play well for 60.” “I think each and every one of us: coaches, staff, players, knows that we have to be one or two plays better,” he continued. “I’ve encouraged the guys to take this time to be one or two plays better, every one of us, so that we can win that game when it comes back in the future.” Kyle Cunanan kicks a PAT last season. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. Even so, Rhule still has confidence in his specialists. NU is just 3-for-7 on field-goal attempts in 2026, but the Huskers' head coach said a strong week of practice would influence his decision to trust the kicking game moving forward. “I don’t know if it was perfect, but that’s one we should make,” said Rhule. “I think we’ve had our share of issues so far… We had a missed extra point against Maryland. We had a bad snap against Maryland… I can’t live in a world of confident (or) not confident. I have to err on the side of going for it.” “If we have a great week of practice, then I’ll lean towards that (kicking),” he continued. “But with Anthony, we basically have been like, ‘Hey, we’re going to try to play four downs’. Not because we don’t trust our field goal game, but because we believe in the weapons we have on offense… But yeah, it’s just something we’ve got to get cleaned up this week before we go to Oregon.” Football out west. 🗓️ 10.17.26 ⏰ 10:00 PM CT 🏟️ Autzen Stadium vs Oregon 📺 @CFBONFOX pic.twitter.com/Cy6UNrS913 Nebraska's game at Oregon will feature the latest kickoff time Rhule has ever coached, with the game certain to extend into the early hours of Sunday morning Central time. To prepare for that, NU is pushing its practices back a two hours and asking players to adjust their sleep schedules. “I had read some of the things that P.J. Fleck had done, I had read some of the things that Charles Huff at Memphis had done, and a lot of it just goes into sleep,” he said. “We’re really asking our guys to go to bed a little bit later each night this week.” “We’re going to finish this game at 2 a.m. our time,” he continued. “Your circadian rhythm starts to shut down, so we’re really just trying, as best as we can, to make 2 a.m. become 12 a.m., make 12 a.m. become 10 p.m. in terms of our bodies this week.” Anthony Colandrea carries the ball against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Having a veteran team likely helps, but so does having a quarterback who sets the tone for the entire team. "I know everything I say gets blown into a little tidbit; I'm not saying he's a Porsche; I'm just saying I think it would be unwise to have a player like Anthony and not let him play to his full ability." picks.blurb: 'An Opportunity Missed': Nebraska Defensive Coordinator Rob Aurich Recaps Indiana Loss, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska had Indiana bottled up until they didn't. College football games last 60 minutes for a reason, and the Cornhuskers ultimately couldn't hold on to a two-possession lead in the fourth quarter. As Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich prepares his unit for a road matchup against a capable Oregon offense Saturday night, he met with the media Tuesday to recap the Blackshirts' performance against the Hoosiers and preview the challenge ahead against the nation's 25th-ranked offense. Aurich knows his defense played well for much of Saturday's game. Even so, he sees an opportunity for the Blackshirts to learn from what went wrong. “An opportunity missed,” he said. “Haunting a little bit, but don’t let the game beat you twice. You take what you can; you learn from it. First year with these guys. I think it’s an excellent opportunity for us to understand what winning time is and how we perform in those moments.” As the Huskers prepare for Oregon, they'll need to make plays in critical moments to have a chance to pull off the upset. Indiana running back Lee Beebe Jr. is tackled by Nebraska defensive lineman Anthony Jones Jr. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Despite the loss, there was plenty that went right for the Big Red. Perhaps the most impressive takeaway was Nebraska's ability to shut down Indiana's running game. Despite the loss, there was plenty that went right for the Big Red. Perhaps the most impressive takeaway was Nebraska's ability to shut down Indiana's running game. “I think we’ve taken steps,” he said. “Fundamentally, you’re seeing us play different coverages at a higher level and have a bunch of answers for some teams with a pretty hefty run game.” “Gonna be another great test this week,” he continued. “I think Oregon has a lot of great tools in the run game that we’re going to have to match up with well. I’m pleased where we are, but I don’t think we’re anywhere near where I think we can be still.” Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola carries the ball against UCLA. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oregon's running back duo of Jordan Davison and Dierre Hill won't be the only matchup for Husker Nation to watch. The two backs have combined for 529 yards and nine rushing touchdowns through five games, but the Ducks also have several quarterback options who could see the field. Oregon's running back duo of Jordan Davison and Dierre Hill won't be the only matchup for Husker Nation to watch. The two backs have combined for 529 yards and nine rushing touchdowns through five games, but the Ducks also have several quarterback options who could see the field. Still, Aurich knows Oregon will maintain its offensive identity regardless of which quarterback earns the start. “At the core of who they are, they’re going to be who they are,” said Aurich. “They’re going to be 11 and 12 (personnel); they’re going to have play actions off of that. They’re going to have a little bit of RPO free access. They want to get their playmakers involved.” “As we navigate each quarterback, I don’t know if it’s necessarily adding this plan to here, but we pull the best matchups from what we plan against all their core stuff,” he continued. “It’s much more of a where on the call sheet are we pulling from rather than a separate plan (for each quarterback).” Ohio wide receiver Eian Pugh is tackled by Nebraska's Jamir Conn. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Like the Ducks, Nebraska is dealing with injuries as it enters the back half of its 2026 schedule. Like the Ducks, Nebraska is dealing with injuries as it enters the back half of its 2026 schedule. Most notably, starting safety Jamir Conn's availability remains a question. On Monday, head coach Matt Rhule called Conn the "lifeblood" of Nebraska's defense . If Conn can't play, Aurich said the solution won't necessarily be as simple as plugging in his backup. In fact, the Big Red may even dabble in different defensive packages. “As we kind of iron out what Jamir’s availability is going to be, if he’s not available, it’s going to be a great test for everybody else in that room,” said Aurich. “Who steps up and how we find the best combination of the best 11 players on the field.” “Let’s say, for whatever reason, someone wasn’t available; it’s not always that we have to replace them with a safety or a corner,” he continued. “What’s the best 11?” Defensive lineman Owen Stoudmire | Nebraska Athletics Given how well Nebraska's defensive line played against Indiana, the Huskers could look to add another player at the line of scrimmage Saturday night. Aurich didn't say that directly, but he praised several defensive linemen for their performances. “He’s the man,” Aurich said of Boston College transfer Owen Stoudmire. “He’s like a centering force of that defensive line. There are a lot of personalities on the defensive line, in a great way, but Owen is just steady, man. He’s steady and doesn’t get moved.” Aurich also praised freshman defensive tackle Dylan Berymon for making an impact in a high-stakes game. “I’m jacked up that he came and impacted us, not in garbage time, in a Big Ten game,” he said. “Really, really pleased with him. The Nebraska Cornhuskers took the defending champion Indiana Hoosiers to the wire, leading for over three quarters before eventually falling 20-17 to the top five team. But sadly, it wasn't meant to be for Anthony Colandrea (pictured above, pointing to Will Compton en route to a 39-yard touchdown that put the Huskers up 17-6, seemingly icing the game for Big Red) and Company, as Herbert Hoover found Nick Marsh for two fourth-quarter scores, keeping the visitors from Bloomington unbeaten. It was, of course, Nebraska's first loss of the season. This team will go the way of its quarterback. How far can Anthony Colandrea carry the Nebraska Cornhuskers? That depends on if every defense will drop eight into coverage and rush three. Three of those eight in coverage are likely SPIES working for the enemy. Well, spies spying on our beloved quarterback. AC also had a few bad throws, struggling to feed his receivers catchable passes. For the first time this season, Nebraska did not throw a touchdown pass. The running game barely scraped by the century mark. Big plays crushed the defense. But if you looked at this game and don't see progress, you're being willfully ignorant. The Huskers controlled the ball, nearly doubling the time of possession. Nebraska was the more physical team, and the defense shut down two prominent opposing rushers. Now Big Red travels to Eugene to face the Oregon Ducks. Oregon just lost to UCLA, benched Dylan Raiola for a former walk-on, and was bumped from the Top 25. Needless to say, it's been a big week for the Ducks. Let's look at what the experts are saying. Vegas oddsmakers believe that this is a much better Nebraska team than what they predicted in the summer. Before the season, the spread for this game was 21.5 points. Immediately after the Nebraska/Indiana game, the spread was 12.5 points. Then Oregon lost to the Bruins. As of this writing, the FanDuel Sportsbook has the home Ducks as a 7.5-point favorite. The Over/Under is currently set at 52.5 points. Put the coffee on for a long night. Nebraska and Oregon kick off at 10:00pm Central Saturday night.

The Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten Conference) and Cornhuskers (5-1, 2-1) will square off at 8 p.m. Oct. 17 in Autzen Stadium with both teams coming off losses. Oregon fell 17-15 to the Bruins at home Saturday. Nebraska lost 20-17 to visiting Indiana as the Hoosiers rallied in the fourth quarter. Here's an early look at the Cornhuskers. (Ben Lonergan/The Register-Guard) 1 / 7 Dan Lanning promises changes to offense, but keeps Oregon plans secret Dan Lanning promises changes to offense, but keeps Oregon plans secret See photos as the Oregon Ducks host the UCLA Bruins at Autzen Stadium Oregon weighing quarterback options as Nebraska game looms Who is Nebraska's QB? Senior Anthony Colandrea has been the starter since transferring from UNLV in the offseason, taking over the position previously held by Oregon backup Dylan Raiola. The 6-foot, 200-pound dual-threat veteran has 37 career starts and was the 2025 Mountain West Conference offensive player of the year. He also spent two seasons at Virginia and was an honorable mention freshman All-American in 2023 at Virginia. In six games this season, Colandrea has completed 119 of 186 passes for 1,405 yards, 13 touchdowns and three interceptions. He's also second on the team in rushing with 296 yards and three scores on 55 carries. Last week against Indiana he was 25-of-43 passing for 264 yards and an interception and rushed 17 times for 47 yards with a 39-yard TD run. Other Nebraska offensive standouts The Cornhuskers' run game is averaging 213.8 and 2.6 TDs per game, and their 39.5 carries per game and 16 rushing touchdowns are second-most in the Big Ten. Freshman Jamal Rule leads the team with 386 yards and five scores in five games. Senior Mekhi Nelson also has 284 yards and four TDs on 60 carries, and nine catches for 148 yards and a TD. Junior Kwazi Gilmer, a transfer from UCLA, is Nebraska's leading receiver with 32 catches for 418 yards and six touchdowns. Junior Jacory Barney Jr. has 27 catches for 341 yards and two touchdowns. He has nine grabs for 108 yards against Indiana last Saturday.
